A1.justification: Both PDFs describe On the Guidance of Flow Matching and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, D4RL planning evaluations, and CelebA-HQ image-restoration experiments, including additional results and an ablation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Equation (2) adds the reverse-coupling ratio P inside the normalizer Z_t, changing the stated general guidance formula when P differs from 1. This is a limited formula correction; the reported P=1 sampling procedures, model components, and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic distribution scenarios, nine D4RL locomotion tasks, and CelebA-HQ central inpainting, fourfold super-resolution, and Gaussian deblurring tasks. Appendix C introduces no coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including CEG in the synthetic comparison, BC and Diffuser in planning, and ΠGDM in image restoration. The compared guidance variants also remain the same.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same training settings, evaluation procedures, and metrics. For example, both report the CelebA-HQ 8:1:1 split, evaluation on 3,000 images, and degradation noise of 0.05.

E4.justification: The Monte Carlo sample-count study in Figure 4, return-distribution analyses in Figures 3 and 5, epsilon ablation in Table 5, and restoration examples in Figures 6–7 are unchanged. The revised theoretical discussion adds no empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeded planning runs and retain the same standard-deviation reporting in Appendix C, including Tables 3–5. No run-count, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing changes are reported.

E6.justification: The experimental values, rankings, curves, and qualitative examples in Tables 1–5 and Figures 2–7 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same gMC average scores of 81.0 for OT-CFM and 79.4 for CFM.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 extends the existing proof to carry P through the guidance derivation and corrects Equation (17). Section 3.3 and Appendix A.8 revise the local-error bound, restoring exponential denominators, adjusting C1/C2, changing the main-text equality to an inequality, and revising the Hessian eigenvalue definition. Appendix A.3 adds an uncoupled-case exception. These are localized mathematical revisions within the retained framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a general guidance framework, asymptotically exact Monte Carlo guidance, training-based guidance, and approximate methods covering classical guidance. The mathematical revisions do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 newly argues that the energy at the estimated sample, J(E[x1]), affects local-guidance accuracy, contrasting estimates in low-energy regions with unreliable gradient exploration at high energy. The existing strong-coupling and Monte Carlo scalability limitations in Appendix B remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix C retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, architectures, hardware, and training-time disclosures. Both PDFs provide the same code-access link; its surrounding grammatical edit does not change access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. The relationships to diffusion guidance, prior flow-matching methods, and existing training losses retain the same substantive positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical edits, revises the covariance-learning explanation in Section 3.3, and adjusts wording in the appendix overview and mathematical discussion. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 slightly reroutes the connector entering the lowest training-loss box without changing the depicted relationship. Revised equations and prose cause local reflow, including moving Equation (79) onto page 23. Experimental figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency by restoring P in the general normalizer and supporting derivation, and correcting factors in the displayed local-error bound. The repair remains incomplete: Appendix A.2's closing definition still omits P, and the prose following Equation (77) retains the earlier bound. These residual inconsistencies limit the gain, but the targeted corrections provide a modest overall improvement.
